WHAT ASTRONAUTS FEEL ON REENTRY

Terry Virts: “The trajectory is set—NASA knows they’re on the RIGHT path.”

“The heat shield and parachutes? Tested—we don’t expect problems.”

“But under those G-FORCES… it’s HARD TO BREATHE.”

“You have to force your chest out—or it feels like getting HIT in the chest.” #artemisII #nasa

Video

REENTRY: NO ROOM FOR ERROR

Les Johnson: “Too steep—they get CRUSHED by G-forces. Too shallow—they SKIP off the atmosphere.”

“The physics is well understood… but space is trying to get you at EVERY TURN.”

“It takes relentless engineering to keep the crew ALIVE and the mission on track.” #artemisII #nasa

Video

“IRAN CAN’T BE TRUSTED”

Brent Sadler:  “There’s not a lot of confidence in any major breakthrough.”

“They keep adding conditions—trying to DISTRACT and build leverage.”

“It’s not clear they’re serious negotiators… they’re NOT TO BE TRUSTED.”

Video

WHAT SETS ASTRONAUTS APART

Dr. Nicky Fox: “They are the BEST OF THE BEST.”

“They are CALM under pressure—that’s what defines them.”

“There’s a calmness from launch to mission control… even when everything’s on the line.” #artemisII #nasa

Video

WHAT ASTRONAUTS ACTUALLY FEEL ON REENTRY

Kjell Lindgren: “They go from 25,000 mph to zero using the atmosphere to slow down.”

“They’ll feel about 4 G-FORCES—four times their body weight—pushing on their chest.”

“It’s the most INTENSE moment of the mission.”
